extracted.intended_audience: authors/writers seeking to market books on TikTok (#BookTok)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical tips and standards for authors who want to use TikTok (#BookTok) to find readers, promote books, and build an author presence. Covers account setup, content types, algorithm behavior, trends, and audience targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the #BookTok hashtag and genre hashtags
rubrics_metrics.description: The hashtag #BookTok opens a doorway to a subsection of TikTok where thousands of voracious readers spend their time, along with #WriterTok and a host of genre hashtags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include #BookTok and relevant genre hashtags on videos to reach the BookTok community; pair with more specific tags (e.g., #GenX, #romance) to niche down and reach target readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat TikTok as a storytelling platform
rubrics_metrics.description: By its very nature, TikTok is a storytelling platform. The videos that reign supreme tell some sort of story, engaging the viewer through drama, comedy, or bewilderment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft videos that convey a narrative or emotional arc—use drama, humor, surprise—to engage viewers rather than just posting flat promotional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be authentic — don’t force silliness
rubrics_metrics.description: You don’t need to do anything that makes you uncomfortable. Be your beautiful, reserved, crazy, funny, introverted, or extroverted self. That’s who readers want to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a genuine persona; authenticity connects with readers more than contrived stunts. If anonymity is needed (e.g., spicy romance), conceal identity appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age is not a barrier
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m too old for TikTok — false. #BookTokers range from 20s to 80s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older authors should not avoid TikTok; the audience spans multiple age brackets and will include your readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: You don’t have to be tech-savvy
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has an advanced video creator built into the app, but it’s very easy to use. They also provide video tutorials. If you still have trouble, head to YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the app’s built-in tutorials or third-party how-to videos; technical barriers are low and surmountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: You don’t have to be comfortable on camera immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: The thought of shooting videos scared me; #BookTok helped me overcome that heart-stopping fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start small, practice, use formats that don’t require on-camera presence (voiceovers, text-over-video, duets), and build confidence over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a personal account (not business) and use your author name
rubrics_metrics.description: I started with a business account, but that was a mistake. Personal accounts get more views. Be sure to use your author name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a personal account for better reach. If you write under multiple pen names, either create separate accounts per pen name or umbrella them under your real name depending on branding strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lurk before posting — learn the rhythm and trends
rubrics_metrics.description: All you’ll be doing at first is lurking. TikTok may seem overwhelming. I did nothing but lurk for a solid month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend weeks observing trends, formats, and language used by successful creators in your genre so your first posts are informed and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train the algorithm by the content you watch
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm throws videos at you, then watches and learns which ones you react to or re-watch. If you stop at every talking dog, the algorithm will flood your For You Page with more talking animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch mostly book- and genre-related content to train your For You Page; consider separate accounts if you want to consume unrelated content without confusing your book-focused feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a link in your bio (LinkTree recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you gain a thousand followers, the link in your bio becomes clickable. Still include one, though. People know to copy/paste a dead link. I use LinkTree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a LinkTree (or similar) in your bio to centralize links to books, website, newsletter, giveaways, etc., even before it’s clickable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay attention to authors in your genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay close attention to authors in your genre. What type of content do they create? Do their videos get a lot of interaction? Do they post only book content? What other type of content do they post? How does their audience react?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study high-performing peers to emulate successful formats, posting cadence, and audience interaction tactics appropriate to your genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use trending sounds, effects, and CapCut templates
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trending Sound could be a fragment of music or a voiceover that helps you connect with an audience. 2024 UPDATE: TikTok also owns CapCut, a video software app. If you use a trending CapCut, you’ll get more views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate trending audio, CapCut templates, and filters where appropriate to increase discoverability; example: a video using a trending CapCut sold 100 books in one day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Duets to expand reach and genre-fit content
rubrics_metrics.description: Duets are when you, well, duet someone else’s video. Romance writers duet male models, paranormal writers duet a medium, serial killer thriller authors duet videos about serial killers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duet relevant creators whose content aligns with your books to reach niche audiences; think creatively about who to duet (e.g., cops for crime writers, librarians for cozies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche down and use demographic hashtags
rubrics_metrics.description: Are your books geared toward an older audience? Use the #GenX hashtag along with a genre hashtag. Are you targeting millennials? Use #GenY. Knowing who your audience is the key to finding potential readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine demographic and genre hashtags to precisely target likely readers and make discovery easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow and engage with other authors — don’t isolate
rubrics_metrics.description: Some authors say never to follow other authors, but that’s a mistake. Writers are your people, your tribe. We learn from each other. We help boost each other’s views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow, comment, and duet with other authors to form a mutual-support network that can amplify visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in or start trends and use filters creatively
rubrics_metrics.description: We also start our own Trends... In this case, the police were searching for a missing person: Grammarly. She named me and a slew of other mystery/thriller authors as possible suspects, and we all created videos of being interrogated by the cops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invent or adapt trends that tie to your books; creative trend participation can result in viral reach and feels less like overt marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie content directly to book elements (characters, motifs, pets)
rubrics_metrics.description: That one video has over 5K views and climbing. It relates to my books because in my Mayhem Series, my antihero has three wild crow companions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagery, props, or themes from your books (characters, animals, settings) to create naturally relevant content that attracts readers of similar tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interact with reviews — duet every review
rubrics_metrics.description: Duet every review. Authors can either “blind react” to a review or prepare themselves first, both done via the Duet feature, helping the review reach more and more readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond publicly to reader reviews via duets to extend the reach of positive reviews and showcase reader reactions to potential buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short, simple videos can be highly effective
rubrics_metrics.description: This video sold 100 books in one day. A video that took me less than one minute to create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don’t need elaborate production—short, on-trend clips can outperform polished long-form videos; prioritize relevance and hook over production time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand genre performance trends on #BookTok
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance (all genres) do the best, followed by fantasy/sci-fi, mystery/thriller/suspense, YA, paranormal, and horror. True crime and nonfiction have their own massive audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use knowledge of which genres perform strongly to set expectations and to tailor content strategy (e.g., romance-friendly formats, thriller hooks).

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok has the highest ROI for selling books (compared to other platforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all the social media sites, X-Twitter has the lowest ROI for selling books. Do you know who has the highest? TikTok.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize time on TikTok if book sales are a key metric; be aware that other platforms may offer lower direct-sales ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to use one or two accounts strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Some authors advise to create two accounts. One to watch animals or whatever. The second for book related content. Alas, I use one account for everything, but I’m cognizant of the type of videos I watch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you consume a lot of unrelated content that could confuse the algorithm, consider maintaining a separate watch-only or personal account to preserve a book-focused For You page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be patient and persistent — finding your groove takes time
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m not sayin’ it’s easy to get started. Finding your groove takes time. But once you get the hang of it, you’ll find your audience much faster than any other social media site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a learning curve; consistent posting, experimentation, and patience are necessary to discover what resonates with your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the platform to show immediate reader reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve never watched a video review of one of your books, you’re missing out... It’s humbling to witness the reaction of a reader who just closed the cover, tears still in her eyes while she gushes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showcase emotional reader reactions to build social proof and connect emotionally with prospective readers.
